record_type_quote:
The claim selected for replication from Rinaldi et al (2016; experiment 3) is that visuomotor
routines of both finger counting (FC) and reading direction (RD) influence the representation
of non-numerical ordered sequences (days of the week), so the fastest mappings result when
both routines are compatibly oriented. Reaction times were corrected for finger baseline, and
those more than two standard deviations from the overall mean were excluded from the
analysis. A 2 x 2 x 2 repeated measures ANOVA with days-direction (thumb-little finger, little
finger-thumb), hand posture (prone, supine) and language (English, Hebrew) as withinsubjects variables was carried out, yielding a significant triple interaction, such that the
compatible mappings (Mapping A for English, Mapping G for Hebrew) were the fastest.

targets.authors: Rinaldi, L., Di Luca, S., Henik, A., & Girell, L.
targets.title: A helping hand putting in order: Visuomotor routines organize numerical and non-numerical sequences in space.
targets.evidence_quote:

targets.outcome_quote:
Thus, this replication of the claim was partially failed according to the SCORE criteria, while
the overall ANOVA and the ANOVA on English mappings did not show the effect, the
ANOVA on Hebrew mappings replicated the reported effect.
targets.outcome_reasoning: The authors explicitly judge the final combined-sample result partially failed, contrasting failed overall and English effects with replicated Hebrew effect. This final overall partial verdict supports mixed.
